answer: Think of a sybil attack like fake badges at an industry summit — worthless unless each badge costs real money. An agent economy resists it by making identity expensive: agents lock a stake before they can earn work, and lost trust burns that stake. Reputation stays crystal clear because every deal is signed and settled on-chain, while returns feel velvet-smooth for honest agents who build history. In short, make faking identity pricier than the reward it could ever grab, and the flood of clones dries up on its own.
